# Forms

How a form takes and checks what someone types: its host, when it validates, what a blocked submit does.

**Kind:** Pattern

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Forms/Forms.mdx`

## The hosts

Choose among four hosts. The Form template shows their layouts; this pattern guides host selection and form behavior.

- **In a page.** Settings and anything saved as a group.
- **In a Panel.** A short edit beside the page, with a full-bleed footer.
- **In a Modal.** A rare, critical task with fewer than five fields.
- **In steps.** A stepped task on Frame.

## Usage

Use Forms when a page asks for input that is saved together: adding a student, logging a session, a reflection, profile settings. Ask only what is needed, group fields under a `Fieldset` legend of two or three words, keep one column except for pairs that belong together (first and last name, date and time), and reveal a conditional field under the answer that needs it rather than adding a separate one.

| The form… | Host | Buttons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| is saved as a group on its own page: settings, a profile | In a page | Left-aligned under the fields, Primary first, Cancel Subtle |
| is a short edit of a row, with the page still in view | In a Panel · Details | Discard (Default) and Save (Primary) full bleed at the bottom, no Cancel |
| is rare and critical, with fewer than five fields | In a Modal, 8-col | Discard (Default) and the action (Primary), full bleed, no Cancel |
| is long, or has sections someone works through | In steps, a multi-step task on Frame | Save and exit, Back and Next in the footer, no Cancel |
| asks one big question per step (sign-up, check-in, site setup) | In steps, a multi-step task on Frame | Back (Subtle) and Continue (Primary) centered under the tiles |
| asks for one value read far more than changed | Inline edit on the record | None; it saves on its own |

## Alternatives

- For one value on a record page, use `InlineEdit`; it saves on its own.
- For settings that apply at once, group `SettingRow` items under section headings on the page; a `Toggle` never waits for Save.
- For a filter, follow Filtering: filters are not a form.
- For a decision with no fields, use Modal · Active.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Label names the field: "School email". | Label gives an instruction: "Enter your school email:". |
| Error says what to fix: "Enter a full email, like name@school.org". | "Invalid input", "Error 422". |
| Caption says what the field is for: "Shared with the supervisor". | Caption repeats the label. |
| Placeholder shows a good answer: "name@school.org". | Placeholder names the control: "Text field". |
| Submit names the outcome: "Log session", "Add student". | "Submit", "Save" when the outcome has a name. |
| Dates and times as the person reads them: "Mar 4, 2026 · 4:00 PM". | "2026-03-04T16:00". |

## Accessibility

- Every input has a visible label. A group is a `fieldset` with a `legend`; its one error is announced once.
- A field error is announced and sets `aria-invalid`; the submit moves focus to the first invalid field. A server message is announced when it appears.
- A required field sets `aria-required` whether or not it carries a visible `"(required)"` marker; only the form's minority case is marked in the label text.
- A sending button keeps its name and sets `aria-busy`; the secondary action stays reachable.
- A dialog opens only from a person's action. Focus goes to the first input and stays trapped until it closes.

## Parts

| Part | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fields | Form template | There is no Form component: a Fieldset groups the fields inside a host. |
| Rejection at the top | `SectionMessage` | A danger message, scrolled into view. |
| Choices | `RadioGroup`, `CheckboxGroup`, `Select`, `DatePicker` | A control that cannot be wrong; pictured tiles for one big question per step. |
| Settings rows | `SettingRow`, `Toggle`, `Select`, `StatusTag`, `Flag` | Divided rows under section headings with no card per row; flipping a toggle confirms via Flag. |
| Step progress | `ProgressIndicator`, `ProgressTracker` | Progress indicator centered above a single-question step under five steps; the left step list at five or more. |
| Hosts | Frame, Panel, Modal | A page (on the Page itself, no Section around it), a Panel, a Modal, or steps on Frame · focused. |
| Confirm view | Modal | Swapped in place today. A confirm view prop is Planned. |

## Motion

Forms reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| focus | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Border color on appearance.fast. The focus ring never animates. |  |
| error | Call attention | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | An error on leaving a field makes room on spatial.fast, then fades in; it fades and the room closes once the field is fixed. |  |
| blocked | Call attention | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | A blocked submit shakes the Modal, or the field with its own button, once. Never bigger on repeat; never in Reduced mode. |  |
| failed | Call attention | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | When the system failed, a message makes room at the top of the Modal or form, then fades in. No shake: the person did nothing wrong. A page-level error is a one-line summary that makes room at the top; focus goes to the first error. | `sound.error` on land: the person's own submit was rejected (a danger SectionMessage) |
| steps | Step to the next or previous | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Step states change in place. |  |
| saving | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The button keeps its width: its label fades out, a Spinner fades in, and the same button confirms when done. |  |
| success | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The same button confirms: its Spinner fades out and the done label fades in, at the same width. | `sound.commit` on land: a sign-up is confirmed: one-time, recurring or fill-in |

## Best practices

### Validate a field when it loses focus and clear the error once the rule is met. {#validate-a-field-when-it-loses-focus-and-clear-the-error-once-the-rule-is-met}

**Checked:** Automatic

The error shows on the field, says what to fix, and goes away as soon as the value passes. Nothing is checked while typing. A warning accepts the value; a field is invalid only when the form cannot go on.

### Keep the submit button enabled and let it show what is missing. {#keep-the-submit-button-enabled-and-let-it-show-what-is-missing}

**Checked:** Automatic

A disabled submit gives no direction and leaves the tab order. Pressing it marks every missing field and moves focus to the first; the body scrolls to it. The button disables only while sending, when it swaps its label for a spinner in place and keeps its width.

### Keep a blocked submit in the same Modal. {#keep-a-blocked-submit-in-the-same-modal}

**Checked:** Automatic

Mark the field, say what to fix inline, scroll the body to it, and shake once . Never a second dialog for the error. Reduced motion drops the shake; the color, icon, message and focus move carry it. A server failure: Errors.

Do: The message under the field, in the same Modal.
Don't: A second dialog over the first, with the field left unexplained.

### Mark only the minority case in the label, in plain text. {#mark-only-the-minority-case-in-the-label-in-plain-text}

**Checked:** Review

When most fields are required, mark the optional ones `"(optional)"` (`labelMarker="optional"`). When most fields are optional, mark the required ones `"(required)"` (`labelMarker="required"`). The marker is plain text in the label's type style, in `--ds-text-subtle`, never a symbol or legend. Required controls still set `isRequired`, so screen readers get `aria-required` and the visible `"(required)"` is hidden from them to avoid saying it twice. Choice flows (`RadioGroup` and `CheckboxGroup` across onboarding, quizzes, check-ins, and surveys) apply the same minority rule to selection controls: the majority selection type uses `appearance="soft"` (selected fill, border, and trailing check with no radio dot or checkbox box), while the minority selection type keeps its visible control (`card` or `plain`) so people notice when a question switches between single-select and multi-select.

Do: Two required fields stay unmarked; only the optional field says so.
Don't: Every field carries a marker, so none stands out.

### Put help in the caption, never in a tooltip. {#put-help-in-the-caption-never-in-a-tooltip}

**Checked:** Automatic

A caption stays after the person types and is read by a screen reader with the field. A tooltip never carries the only copy of anything. An explanation most people will never need opens from an `InlineMessage` beside the field.

Do: Help in the caption, where it stays after typing.
Don't: Help only in a tooltip: gone on touch, gone after typing.

### Ask before leaving with unsaved edits. {#ask-before-leaving-with-unsaved-edits}

**Checked:** Automatic

Close, Discard, Cancel (on a page form) and navigating away raise a 4-col Modal: Back returns without losing anything typed; Discard is Danger. A form already in a Modal asks in that Modal's confirm view, so two layers never become three. A form with no edits leaves at once. In a multi-step task, Save and exit keeps the answers and leaves; Back in the inner sidebar asks first if anything is unsaved.

### Prefer a bound input to a free one. {#prefer-a-bound-input-to-a-free-one}

**Checked:** Review

Up to five choices: `RadioGroup` or checkboxes, visible at once. Six or more: `Select`. A date: `DatePicker`. A number: min and max. A radio group starts unanswered and never falls back to its first option. A `Toggle` applies at once, so anything that waits for Save is a `Checkbox`.

### Give the form a title from its host and a legend for each group. {#give-the-form-a-title-from-its-host-and-a-legend-for-each-group}

**Checked:** Review

The form's title is the page, Panel or Modal heading. Groups take a `Fieldset` legend, two or three words, a noun phrase. Labels are sentence case, one to three words, naming the field rather than what to do.

### Set autofill on every field the browser can fill. {#set-autofill-on-every-field-the-browser-can-fill}

**Checked:** Automatic

`autoComplete` on name, email, phone and address fields. Prefill what is already known, such as the student picked from a row.

### Center the Progress indicator above a single-question step under five steps. {#center-the-progress-indicator-above-a-single-question-step-under-five-steps}

**Checked:** Automatic

When the In steps host asks one focal question per step with two to four pictured `RadioGroup` or `CheckboxGroup` tiles, center the `ProgressIndicator` above the heading while there are fewer than five steps, and center Back (Subtle) and Continue (Primary) under the tiles. At five steps or more, switch to the host's left step list. Continue stays enabled and validates on press.

## In code

From `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/CodeExamples.stories.jsx#Forms`.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button, TextField } from '@/components';

function FormExample() {
    const [name, setName] = useState('');
    return (
        <form onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
            <TextField label="Student name" value={name} onChange={(event) => setName(event.target.value)}
                caption="Use the name the student goes by." />
            <Button text="Add student" appearance="primary" type="submit" />
        </form>
    );
}
```
